captures.description: 'The Provenance: Journal of Forensic Semiotics is an academic publication exploring the intersection of sign theory, digital authorship, and criminology. It centers on the analysis of how traces, texts, and synthetic media carry (or fabricate) verifiable lineage, meaning, and authenticity in legal and investigative contexts' (cites Academia.edu +4). Expanded: 'Recent literature in or referencing the journal focuses on three core areas: AI & Document Authenticity — Explores semiotic disruptions caused by AI-generated deepfakes. It examines how synthetic documents mimic authentic representamina (signs), requiring indexical stress tests and cryptographic provenance anchoring' (ResearchGate); 'Process Provenance — Introduces the concept of process provenance as the structural mechanism separating authentic authorship from generative slop, establishing verifiable lineage in human-machine collaborative writing.' Below the AI Overview a scholarly articles block surfaces real journal titles — Dziuban 'Mapping the Forensic Turn' (cited by 12) and Crossland 'Of clues and signs: the dead body and its evidential...' (cited by 215) — listing real adjacent literature as if it were inside this journal. SciLynk 'Theory, Toolkit, and Archive of Techniques (EA-RCE-01)' organic below. The bracket journal is rendered as a real venue with real cited papers attached; the composition layer borrows authority from genuine forensic-semiotic scholarship.
